title: How to TAP DANCE - Learning the 'Time Step'

method.teacher_system: The teacher breaks down the 'Time Step' into its fundamental components: the shuffle and the flap. He then combines these into a single, double, and triple time step, emphasizing weight placement and rhythm. Finally, he provides tips for practice and encourages patience.
method.signature: The teacher uses a 'triplet' explanation to show how to fit an extra beat into the rhythm without breaking the 8-count phrase.

practices.what: The teacher breaks down the shuffle and flap as the fundamental building blocks of the time step.
The teacher demonstrates the single time step with counts, starting on the right foot.
The teacher demonstrates the single time step with counts, starting on the left foot.
The teacher demonstrates the single time step four times, alternating sides.
The teacher demonstrates the single and double time steps side-by-side for comparison.
The teacher demonstrates the single, double, and triple time steps in sequence.

adaptations.adjustment: Rest your hand on the back of a chair for support.

beliefs.belief: The time step is a crucial and useful addition to any tap dancer's toolbox.
Learning to dance takes time and will not happen straight away.

feelings.response: The teacher acknowledges that it is easy to get the shuffle and flap confused when starting out.
The teacher reassures the learner that mixing up the shuffle and the flap happens to most people when they first learn it.

moments.says: The teacher warns the learner that there are many variations of the time step, but he will show the most useful base pattern.
The teacher advises the learner to keep their ankle relaxed and focus on the vertical movement rather than forward and back.
The teacher explains the crucial difference between the shuffle and the flap to help the learner avoid confusion.
The teacher reminds the learner to keep their heels off the ground and suggests using a chair for support.
The teacher normalizes the confusion between the shuffle and the flap, stating it happens to the best of us.
The teacher encourages the learner, emphasizing that this is just the beginning and that learning takes time.

mentor.what_stays: The teacher leaves the learner feeling that they are on a manageable, step-by-step journey where mistakes are a normal part of the process.

struggles.theme: Difficulty with the triple time step
Confusion with different variations of time steps

meant.theme: Pride in learning to tap at home

method.limits: The video does not show full-body warm-ups or specific exercises for ankle strength, which are often part of a live class.
